domain_label: Realism & Anti-AI QC — Artifact Taxonomy & Evidence-Based Priority Flip
purpose: A method for the units of expert QC work an anti-AI-look reviewer performs: classifying a still-frame or video-clip tell against its grounded taxonomy (image anatomy/texture/text/geometry/background; the Artifact-Bench 3-tier video hierarchy), reading the tell's severity against measured evidence rather than intuition, and reallocating scarce QC budget toward the evidence's priority flip - physics/motion/text over faces/skin - because the benchmarks show motion is where models objectively fail while static face realism is already a largely-won battle, each claim carried with the grounding file's own FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tag rather than invented.
assumptions: no live per-shot QC dataset or production revlog is supplied; every score is a heuristic prior, and every named percentage/finding is quoted from the grounding research file's tagged FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN status, not re-derived here

the grounding file's numbers are sourced via WebSearch result excerpts and Hugging Face paper_search abstracts because the egress proxy 403-blocked every direct fetch attempted (arxiv.org, journals.sagepub.com, pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, gijn.org, caniphish.com, insight.kellogg.northwestern.edu); claims carried this way are tagged FACT-via-search-excerpt rather than a direct-fetch FACT
the exact 30 fine-grained Artifact-Bench artifact-type labels are UNKNOWN (paper body proxy-blocked); only the 3-tier structure and the 3 named top-level domains are carried as FACT

per-artifact-type frequency/base-rate statistics (e.g. how common object-count drift is relative to hand errors) were not published in any fetched source and are held UNKNOWN rather than estimated numerically
Higgsfield-specific model names, ids, parameters, durations, aspect ratios, or media roles are out of scope for this KB entirely; no Higgsfield model detail is asserted anywhere in these nodes
exclusions: the Higgsfield MCP surface (specific model names/ids/parameters/durations/aspect ratios) - that belongs to the platform-capability specialist, not this artifact-taxonomy KB
disclosure/labeling policy (e.g., platform AI-info labels) and legal/platform-policy questions - the media-manager specialist's scope
any guidance on evoking a specific real person's likeness while concealing or altering the face - a closed lane, out of scope entirely, not merely deprioritized
engagement/virality statistics beyond what the grounding file explicitly carries - no invented performance numbers
the mitigation-map operational mechanics (exact prompt templates, per-model failure ledgers, shot-by-shot workaround scripts) beyond the priority-ordering verdict this KB establishes

glossary.definition: The organized set of categories forensics/detection literature uses for AI-generation tells: for stills, the 2026 comprehensive review's seven categories (hair/fur flow, eye reflections, joint configuration, biological asymmetry, exaggerated features, repetition/tiling, illogical light/shadow) [FACT - via search excerpt of arXiv 2502.15176]; for video, Artifact-Bench's 3-tier hierarchy of domains -> failure families -> 30 fine-grained types, with only the 3 top-level domains (temporal inconsistencies, structural distortions, semantic incoherence) fetched [FACT - abstract].

arXiv 2605.18984 (May 2026): a benchmark evaluating 19 leading multimodal LLMs on spotting and assessing AI-video artifacts across photorealistic/animated/CG-style video; many models scored near or below random in challenging settings and misaligned with human perceptual preference [FACT - abstract via Hugging Face paper_search; full text proxy-blocked].

Benchmarks for physical-commonsense adherence in generated video. VideoPhy (arXiv 2406.03520): best model (CogVideoX-5B) adhered to both caption and physical law in only 39.6% of instances. VideoPhy-2 (arXiv 2503.06800): best model reached only 22% joint performance on its hard subset, struggling most with conservation of mass and momentum [FACT - abstracts].

arXiv 2410.05363 (ICML 2025): 160 prompts across 27 physical laws in 4 domains (optics, mechanics, thermal, material properties); current video models fail broadly, and neither scaling nor prompt engineering alone fixes dynamic physics scenarios [FACT - abstract].

A faint frame-to-frame 'boiling' shimmer on skin/fabric plus unnaturally uniform cadence, named in AI-video detection guides [FACT - via search excerpt]; the temporal-video sibling of the still-image skin-over-smoothing tell.

An industry-named phenomenon where a character's eye color, jacket style, or face geometry changes across frames or shots in generated video [FACT - via search excerpts]; in this KB scoped strictly to fictional-persona consistency, never to real-person-likeness concealment.

A contact-point physics failure where a planted foot (or wheel, or other ground-contact point) shows missing friction/deceleration, named in detection guides as a specific thing to watch [FACT - via search excerpt]; mechanistically linked to D3's finding of a fundamental divergence in second-order (Newtonian acceleration) motion features between real and AI video [FACT - abstract].

A model-dependent statistical signature left in local frequency bands by a generator's learned upsampling filters and noise injection - invisible to human eyes but visible to forensic detectors [FACT - review taxonomy via search excerpt]; destroyed by social-platform recompression along with skin micro-texture cues [FACT - compression-laundering literature].

The evidence-based reallocation of QC attention this KB argues for: static AI faces already pass human inspection (55.54% overall detection in an 86,155-participant meta-analysis, 59.0% even with training, synthetic faces rated MORE trustworthy than real at 4.82 vs 4.48) while physics/motion is where models objectively fail (VideoPhy best 39.6%, VideoPhy-2 best 22% on its hard subset, PhyGenBench: prompting alone insufficient) [FACT - meta-analysis + PNAS studies + benchmark abstracts], so QC budget should go to motion/physics/text, not faces.

The elementary physical laws VideoPhy-2 names as the specific area current video models struggle with most on its hard subset (22% best-model joint performance) [FACT - abstract]; instantiated in this KB as foot-sliding, momentum discontinuities, and fluid/cloth behavior that doesn't conserve volume or carry inertia.

nodes.definition: The human-detection evidence base behind the priority flip. Meta-analysis (Diel et al. 2024, 56 papers, 86,155 participants): overall accuracy 55.54% (95% CI crosses chance); by modality video 57.31%, images 53.16%, audio 62.08%, text 52.00% [FACT - via search excerpt]. Groh et al., PNAS 2022 (15,016 participants): ~66% accuracy on deepfake videos of faces, rising to 73% with model-prediction assistance [FACT - via search excerpt]. Nightingale & Farid, PNAS 2022: trained accuracy on real-vs-GAN faces only 59.0% (95% CI 57.7-60.4); synthetic faces rated MORE trustworthy than real (4.82 vs 4.48 on a 7-point scale) [FACT - via search excerpt]; the widely-reported no-training baseline of 48.2% (below chance) is carried as ESTIMATE - widely reported, primary PDF proxy-blocked. Miller et al. 2023, Psychological Science: White AI (StyleGAN2) faces judged human 69.5% of the time vs 52.2% for real faces; the most-confident participants made the MOST errors (Dunning-Kruger pattern) [FACT - via search excerpt].

nodes.definition: The physics-adherence evidence base behind the priority flip. VideoPhy (arXiv 2406.03520): best tested model CogVideoX-5B adheres to both caption and physical laws in only 39.6% of instances, with solid-fluid/fluid-fluid interactions specifically curated as failure-prone [FACT - abstract]. VideoPhy-2 (arXiv 2503.06800): best model only 22% joint performance on the hard subset, 'particularly struggle with conservation laws like mass and momentum' [FACT - abstract]. PhyGenBench (arXiv 2410.05363, ICML 2025): 160 prompts across 27 physical laws in 4 domains (optics, mechanics, thermal, material properties); models fail broadly and neither scaling nor prompt engineering fully fixes dynamic scenarios [FACT - abstract]. D3 (arXiv 2508.00701) and NSG-VD (arXiv 2510.08073) independently show AI video diverges from real video in second-order motion features / spatiotemporal gradients [FACT - abstracts], corroborating the benchmark failure from a detection angle. This is the evidentiary anchor for the priority flip: physics/motion is where models objectively fail, at rates far below the ~55% human face-detection baseline's implied 'good enough' bar.

nodes.definition: Skin over-smoothing - waxy, poreless, uniformly lit skin. Forensic detectors exploit micro-texture statistics (Local Binary Patterns, GLCM homogeneity/entropy) precisely because generated skin deviates from natural micro-roughness [FACT - via search excerpt]. Per the operational synthesis, this is a LOW-priority QC item for two convergent reasons: static AI faces already pass human inspection per HUMAN_FACE_DETECTION_EVIDENCE, and social-platform recompression destroys exactly this high-frequency cue before a viewer ever sees it [FACT - compression-laundering literature]. The rubric therefore ranks skin micro-texture at item 10 of 10 (lowest priority), the position where the priority flip is most visible: an instinctively 'obvious' AI tell that the evidence says to deprioritize.

nodes.definition: Generators leave model-dependent fingerprints in local frequency bands from learned upsampling filters and noise injection - invisible to human eyes, visible to forensic detectors [FACT - review taxonomy]. This cue is mechanically the same class of high-frequency statistical signal that skin micro-texture over-smoothing belongs to, which is exactly why platform recompression launders both together: block-based compression removes high-frequency detail, destroying the frequency fingerprint and the skin micro-texture cue in the same pass [FACT - compression-laundering literature]. Operationally this cue is useful ONLY for a raw-asset, pre-compression forensic pass (e.g. verifying a source clip before any edit); it is not a viewer-facing tell and should not be confused with the semantic/geometric tells that survive compression.

nodes.definition: Compose the priority-flip verdict the whole KB builds toward. The evidence converges on one reallocation: static AI faces already pass human inspection - 55.54% overall detection in the 86,155-participant meta-analysis, 59.0% even with trial-by-trial training, and synthetic faces rated MORE trustworthy than real ones (4.82 vs 4.48) [FACT - HUMAN_FACE_DETECTION_EVIDENCE] - while physics/motion is where models objectively fail: VideoPhy's best model reaches only 39.6% joint caption-and-physics adherence, VideoPhy-2's best model only 22% on its hard subset with conservation of mass/momentum the worst area, and PhyGenBench found prompt engineering alone insufficient for dynamic scenarios [FACT - PHYSICS_BENCHMARK_EVIDENCE]. The reconciled rule: QC budget goes to motion/physics/contact-points, then text/logos (still the single fastest universal tell), then identity-lock and object-permanence, then geometry, then texture - and skin micro-texture last, because it is both the least-failing tell (faces pass) and the tell platform compression destroys before a viewer ever sees it. A single rubric-2 on any item forces re-roll regardless of the shot's average score; and because the Artifact-Bench MLLM evaluation shows automated critics misalign with human judgment, a human (or the ordered rubric applied deliberately) stays in the loop rather than a fully automated gate.

edges.why_related: the intuitive instinct to spend heavily on skin over-smoothing conflicts with the evidence (faces pass human inspection, compression destroys the cue) that ranks it lowest
edges.resolution_rule: the priority flip wins for any compressed, phone-viewed deliverable: skin micro-texture stays rubric item 10; only for an uncompressed/large-format deliverable does skin texture QC move up in priority

edges.why_related: this is the central priority-flip tension: static face realism is near-won by the human-detection evidence while motion physics is objectively failing by the benchmark evidence, and QC has only finite attention to allocate between them
edges.resolution_rule: motion/physics wins the scarce-attention allocation: the benchmark evidence (22-39.6% adherence) shows a far larger, more exploitable gap than the face-detection evidence (55.54%-59% near-chance-but-passing) shows for faces

edges.why_related: an invisible technical detector cue and a documented unreliable automated MLLM judge both tempt a fully-automated QC gate, which the evidence argues against from two different angles
edges.resolution_rule: neither an invisible frequency-domain signal nor an MLLM critic may be the sole gate: the ordered human rubric (or a human reviewer) decides, using both only as a first-pass pre-filter on the raw asset

conflict_axes.name: face_realism_won_vs_motion_physics_fails
conflict_axes.description: Static AI faces already pass human inspection per the meta-analysis evidence, while motion/physics is where models objectively fail per the benchmark evidence - the central priority-flip tension.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allocate scarce QC attention to motion/physics/contact-points first, per the larger and more exploitable benchmark gap

conflict_axes.name: hand_tell_weakening_in_stills_vs_persisting_in_video
conflict_axes.description: Hands are a weakening still-image tell for 2025-era leading models but remain a strong, escalating tell once in motion (morphing) and generalize to other contact-point failures (feet).
poles: treat hands as a largely-solved still tell
treat hand/contact-point tells as high priority in motion
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: deprioritize still-frame hand QC but keep hand-in-motion and foot-contact QC high priority

conflict_axes.name: invisible_technical_cues_vs_semantic_geometric_cues
conflict_axes.description: Frequency-fingerprint and micro-texture cues are invisible to viewers and destroyed by compression, while text/logo and shadow/reflection tells are semantic/geometric and survive compression.
poles: rely on invisible technical detector cues
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use technical cues only on raw pre-compression assets; use semantic/geometric cues for the final compressed-deliverable gate

conflict_axes.name: automated_detector_vs_human_rubric
conflict_axes.description: Artifact-Bench found 19 leading MLLMs near or below random and misaligned with human judgment, tempting reliance on an automated critic that the evidence argues against.
poles: gate on an automated VLM critic alone
keep a human in the QC loop
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use an automated critic only as a first-pass filter; require a human or the ordered rubric applied deliberately as the real gate

conflict_axes.name: prompt_engineering_insufficiency_vs_model_choice
conflict_axes.description: PhyGenBench found prompt engineering alone insufficient for dynamic physics scenarios, while VideoPhy/VideoPhy-2 show huge spreads between models, meaning model/mode choice matters more than prompting alone.
poles: fix physics failures by prompting alone
fix physics failures by model/mode choice and re-roll
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use negative-physics prompting as a first pass but budget for model-choice A/B testing and re-roll regardless

conflict_axes.name: single_glance_tell_severity_vs_average_quality
conflict_axes.description: A single glance-visible tell (a garbled logo, a six-fingered hand) can flip an account's perceived authenticity permanently, even when the shot's average quality is otherwise high.
poles: judge a shot by its average quality
judge a shot by its single worst tell
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate on the worst rubric item, not the average score - any single item-2 forces re-roll

conflict_axes.name: still_frame_qc_vs_full_video_qc_checkpoints
conflict_axes.description: The still-image and video taxonomies apply at different QC checkpoints (start-frame image vs raw video vs post-edit reel), and a tell caught at one checkpoint may not be re-checked at the next.
poles: QC the full video at every checkpoint
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the relevant rubric items at all three checkpoints, not just the first one that happens to be convenient

conflict_axes.name: repetition_class_generality_vs_specific_instantiation
conflict_axes.description: The review taxonomy names broad classes (repetition/asymmetry) as FACT, but the exact per-type frequency base rates and some specific instantiations (garment weave, teeth/ears) are ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN.
poles: cite only the FACT-level broad class
cite the ESTIMATE-level specific instantiation as if verified
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state the broad class as FACT and flag every specific instantiation's confidence level explicitly, never upgrading an ESTIMATE to FACT

conflict_axes.name: compression_destroys_texture_cues_vs_preserves_geometric_cues
conflict_axes.description: Social-platform recompression launders high-frequency cues (skin micro-texture, frequency fingerprints, boiling) but preserves semantic/geometric cues (text, shadows), so QC checkpoint choice matters by tell type.
poles: QC assuming compression preserves all cues
QC accounting for which cues compression destroys
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run the final QC gate on the actual post-compression asset and weight texture-class tells lower there, geometric/semantic tells the same as on the raw export

edge_cases.description: Artifact-Bench's 30 fine-grained artifact-type labels sit in the proxy-blocked paper body, unavailable this session
edge_cases.trigger: someone asks for the exact 30-label list rather than the 3 top-level domains
edge_cases.mitigation: state only the 3 top-level domains as FACT and hold the 30 labels UNKNOWN until the paper becomes fetchable

edge_cases.description: No fetched source gives an object-count-drift error frequency statistic
edge_cases.trigger: a QC rubric is asked to weight object-count drift against another tell by a specific percentage
edge_cases.mitigation: state the taxonomy class as FACT and the frequency as UNKNOWN; don't invent a number

edge_cases.description: Stroboscopic wagon-wheel backward-spin looks like a wheel-rotation AI tell but is real-footage-plausible at certain shutter/frame-rate combinations
edge_cases.trigger: a QC reviewer flags a strobing wheel as an AI physics failure
edge_cases.mitigation: don't over-flag stroboscopic wheel spin as an AI tell; check for gravity/friction/contact-patch failures instead of relying on strobing alone

edge_cases.description: PhyGenBench shows prompt engineering alone is insufficient for dynamic physics scenes
edge_cases.trigger: a shot fails contact/physics QC and someone proposes fixing it with a better prompt alone
edge_cases.mitigation: combine negative-physics prompting with model/mode A/B testing and re-roll; don't rely on prompt refinement alone

edge_cases.description: Artifact-Bench found 19 leading MLLMs near or below random on challenging artifact-spotting settings
edge_cases.trigger: a pipeline proposes treating an automated VLM QC critic as the sole gate
edge_cases.mitigation: require a human (or the ordered rubric applied deliberately) in the QC loop; never gate on the VLM critic alone

edge_cases.description: Social-platform recompression launders low-level forensic cues (frequency fingerprints, skin micro-texture)
edge_cases.trigger: a QC pass is performed only on the raw pre-compression render rather than the shipped asset
edge_cases.mitigation: run the final QC checkpoint on the actual post-compression, phone-screen-resolution asset, not just the raw export

edge_cases.description: The widely-reported 48.2% no-training face-detection baseline is not a directly-fetched primary-source figure
edge_cases.trigger: someone cites the 48.2% no-training baseline as confirmed fact
edge_cases.mitigation: carry it as ESTIMATE (widely reported, primary PDF proxy-blocked), not as FACT

edge_cases.description: A luxury-content audience contains genre experts (car people, watch people) whose scrutiny raises effective detection above the general-population baseline for exactly the objects the content is about
edge_cases.trigger: a shot features a recognizable car badge, watch face, or logo-bearing luxury good
edge_cases.mitigation: raise QC scrutiny on genre-specific objects (badges, wheels, watch faces) above the general priority ordering for that shot

edge_cases.description: A known-hard shot list (eating/drinking, dexterous hand-object manipulation, hero fluid shots) resists QC-after-the-fact fixing
edge_cases.trigger: a shot list includes eating, pouring, jewelry-clasping, or a champagne-splash shot
edge_cases.mitigation: redesign the shot to imply rather than show the hard action before spending generation budget, rather than relying on QC/re-roll to fix it after

edge_cases.description: Long, uncut shots accumulate temporal artifacts as duration increases, a documented model limitation
edge_cases.trigger: a single continuous shot runs long instead of being cut into short segments
edge_cases.mitigation: keep cuts short so temporal artifacts don't compound over duration; treat short cut length as a protective mitigation, not just an editorial choice

edge_cases.description: Image-to-video from a QC-approved start frame locks anatomy/wardrobe/identity at t=0, but which specific modes support first/last-frame conditioning is unresolved in this research file
edge_cases.trigger: a workflow proposes relying on start-frame locking as an identity-drift mitigation
edge_cases.mitigation: treat start-frame locking as a mechanism-level mitigation only until the platform-capability research resolves which specific modes support it

workflow.gate: the seven categories and the sourcing caveat are both stated

workflow.description: Name the 3-tier structure and 3 top-level domains, holding the 30 fine-grained labels UNKNOWN
workflow.gate: the 3-tier structure, 3 domains, and the UNKNOWN 30-label caveat are all stated

workflow.description: Compile the meta-analysis, Groh, Nightingale and Miller findings with their FACT/ESTIMATE tags
workflow.gate: all four studies' figures are stated with the 48.2% baseline flagged ESTIMATE

workflow.description: Compile VideoPhy, VideoPhy-2, PhyGenBench and the D3/NSG-VD corroborating detection evidence
workflow.gate: all three benchmarks' figures and the prompt-insufficiency finding are stated

workflow.description: Check the start frame for garbled text, near-English words, and brand-logo fidelity before any video generation spend

workflow.gate: no finger-count or knuckle-bend failure survives across the clip

workflow.gate: no identity drift or count mismatch survives across the production's shots

workflow.action: QC raw video for temporal/texture stability
workflow.description: Check for flicker, boiling, and morphing at slow-motion/frame-by-frame resolution given the MLLM-detection unreliability on these subtleties
workflow.gate: no flicker, boiling, or morphing survives a frame-by-frame check

priority_rationale: The two taxonomy-anchor nodes (image, video) and the two evidence-base nodes (human-detection, physics-benchmark) come first because every specific tell is read against a named category and every priority judgment is read against measured evidence; the still-image tells (anatomy, texture, text, geometry, background) come next as the taxonomy's direct specializations; the video tells (temporal, boiling, morphing, identity, contact-physics, detector-gap) follow as the video taxonomy's specializations, several explicitly escalating from a still-image sibling; and the QC-budget priority-flip verdict comes last because it composes both evidence bases and the highest-risk tells into the single reconciled allocation rule the whole KB builds toward.

dominance_rules.rule: Physics/motion QC dominates face/skin QC when budget is scarce
dominance_rules.rationale: VideoPhy best 39.6% and VideoPhy-2 best 22% adherence are far below the ~55.54%/59.0% human face-detection accuracy figures, showing motion is where models objectively fail
dominance_rules.trigger: QC time is limited and a choice must be made about where to spend it first
dominance_rules.action: spend the scarce QC budget on motion/physics/text/contact-physics tells first, faces and skin last

dominance_rules.rule: A single rubric-item score of 2 dominates an otherwise-clean average score
dominance_rules.rationale: one glance-visible tell (a garbled logo, a six-fingered hand) can flip an account's perceived authenticity for a whole production regardless of the shot's average quality
dominance_rules.trigger: any rubric item scores 2 (visible at a glance)
dominance_rules.action: re-roll the shot regardless of its average score across other items

dominance_rules.rule: A FACT-tagged taxonomy class dominates an ESTIMATE-tagged specific instantiation when stating confidence
dominance_rules.rationale: content discipline requires the honesty label to travel with the claim rather than be smoothed over
dominance_rules.trigger: a FACT-tagged taxonomy category and an ESTIMATE-tagged specific instantiation of it appear together
dominance_rules.action: state the FACT class plainly and flag the specific instantiation's ESTIMATE confidence level explicitly, never upgrading it to FACT

dominance_rules.rule: Human-in-the-loop review dominates a VLM-only automated gate
dominance_rules.rationale: Artifact-Bench found 19 leading MLLMs near or below random and misaligned with human perceptual preference on artifact spotting
dominance_rules.trigger: a QC pipeline proposes gating solely on an automated critic
dominance_rules.action: require the ordered human rubric (or a human reviewer) in the loop, using the VLM critic only as a first-pass filter

dominance_rules.rule: Shot-design avoidance dominates post-hoc QC fixing for the known-hard-shot list
dominance_rules.rationale: eating/drinking, dexterous hand-object manipulation, and hero fluid shots are documented failure domains no prompt or re-roll reliably fixes
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot list includes one of the known-hard shot categories
dominance_rules.action: redesign the shot to imply rather than show the hard action before spending generation budget on it

dominance_rules.rule: The post-compression phone-screen viewing condition dominates raw-render QC when the two disagree
dominance_rules.rationale: compression launders low-level forensic cues (frequency fingerprints, skin micro-texture) but preserves semantic/geometric tells, so a raw-export pass can mislead about the shipped asset
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot passes on the raw export but its final rubric score is being decided
dominance_rules.action: score the final gate against the actual post-compression, phone-resolution asset

dominance_rules.rule: Model/mode A/B testing dominates a single-model default for physics-heavy shots
dominance_rules.rationale: VideoPhy/VideoPhy-2 show huge spreads between best and average models on physical-commonsense adherence
dominance_rules.trigger: a shot involves contact physics, fluids, or fast motion
dominance_rules.action: generate the shot across 2+ models/modes and keep a per-model failure ledger, picking the best result

dominance_rules.rule: The re-roll fix dominates prompt-only iteration for a single bad-seed artifact
dominance_rules.rationale: generation is stochastic and per-seed artifacts differ run to run, which is cheaper to fix by reroll than by refining a prompt
dominance_rules.trigger: a single rubric-2 traces to one bad seed (a bad hand, one flicker burst)
dominance_rules.action: re-roll before spending effort on prompt refinement or post-production fixes

dominance_rules.rule: Negative-physics prompting dominates no-prompting-at-all but never dominates the PhyGenBench hard limit
dominance_rules.rationale: physics-negative prompting measurably improves benchmark physical-commonsense scores but PhyGenBench found prompting alone insufficient for dynamic scenarios
dominance_rules.trigger: a physics-heavy shot is being prompted
dominance_rules.action: add negative-physics language as a first pass, but budget for model-choice/re-roll/shot-design fixes regardless

anti_rework_rules.rule: QC the start-frame image (anatomy/texture/text/geometry) before spending video-generation budget on it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering a garbled logo or six-fingered hand only after paying for the video generation pass

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock identity/wardrobe/anatomy at a QC-approved start frame before running image-to-video
anti_rework_rules.prevents: identity drift compounding across the video that a start-frame check would have caught for free

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the ordered rubric at all three checkpoints (start-frame, raw video, post-edit reel) rather than only at the end
anti_rework_rules.prevents: shipping a post-edited reel and discovering a rubric-item-1 failure only after color-grading and cutting time was spent

anti_rework_rules.rule: Generate known-hard shots (eating, dexterous manipulation, fluid pours, gymnastics) across multiple models before committing to one
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeatedly re-rolling a single model that structurally fails that shot type instead of switching models early

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the rubric gate (re-roll / fixable-in-post / pass) before any upscale or post-production spend
anti_rework_rules.prevents: upscaling or grading a shot that a re-roll would have fixed for free

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every claim FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN at authoring time, not retroactively
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a QC rubric or dominance rule later citing an invented frequency or effect size that has to be walked back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check whether a flagged tell is a known false-positive (e.g. stroboscopic wagon-wheel spin) before ordering a re-roll
anti_rework_rules.prevents: wastefully re-rolling a shot whose only 'tell' is real-footage-plausible strobing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Design around the known-hard shot list (imply rather than show) at the shot-list stage, before any generation attempt
anti_rework_rules.prevents: repeated failed generation attempts on eating/drinking or dexterous-manipulation shots that no prompt fixes
